messages:
olivia: Hi all, first day here! I'm able to ssh to bastion-apac-1 but `docker pull repo.corp.redwood:5000/myimage:latest` from my MacBook Air (M2, macOS 13) times out. Internal docs load over browser but the registry hangs. Anyone run into Docker + WireGuard split-tunnel issues?
marta: welcome :wave: Are you using the WireGuard profile from onboarding (split-tunnel)?
olivia: yeah, default profile. DNS resolves repo.corp.redwood to 10.45.10.50, `ping 10.45.10.50` from terminal works, but `docker pull` stalls at "Waiting for headers".
infra-bot: provisioned: user/olivia added to bastion-apac-1
martA (typo corrected): small Q: does `docker run --rm -it --network host alpine:3.18 nslookup repo.corp.redwood` show the internal DNS?
olivia: ran that, got `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached`. But `scutil --dns` shows the corp resolver 10.45.1.10 present.
devx: Docker Desktop on mac uses its own internal VM for containers which doesn't always inherit macOS split-tunnel DNS routes. Two common fixes:
1) Configure Docker daemon to use the corporate DNS: create or edit `~/.docker/daemon.json` (or `/etc/docker/daemon.json` depending on setup) with:
```
{
  "dns": ["10.45.1.10", "1.1.1.1"]
}
```
then restart Docker Desktop.
2) Add an entry to /etc/hosts mapping repo.corp.redwood to 10.45.10.50 as a temporary workaround: `sudo -- sh -c 'echo "10.45.10.50 repo.corp.redwood" >> /etc/hosts'`
(3) As a longer-term fix, enable "Send All Traffic" (full-tunnel) on the WireGuard profile for macOS if allowed by policy so the Docker VM uses the same routes.
olivia: tried adding daemon.json and restarted Docker Desktop. `docker pull` progressed past headers but then failed with TLS handshake error: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` (it's a self-signed cert on the internal registry).
marta: oh right, internal registry uses our internal CA. You need to add the CA to Docker's trusted certs. On mac: add the CA cert to macOS Keychain (System) and mark it trusted for SSL, then restart Docker Desktop. Alternatively for the registry only, add the CA to Docker's certs dir: `~/Library/Group\ Containers/group.com.docker/devicemapper/certs.d/repo.corp.redwood:5000/ca.crt` (path varies by Docker version).
olivia: added CA to keychain, trusted it, restarted Docker Desktop, and `docker pull` now works! :tada:
devx: sweet. We'll add this to the onboarding doc: note about Docker Desktop not inheriting split-tunnel DNS, steps to set daemon DNS and install internal CA, plus fallback of /etc/hosts.
it-support: filing ticket ONB-412: "Mac + Docker Desktop: registry access steps for new hires (WireGuard split-tunnel)" and assigning to devx.
olivia: one last Q: is there a recommended way to access the registry from CI runners? Our GitHub Actions sometimes used the public DNS and get rate-limited.
marta: internal CI runners are in the VPC so they resolve 10.45.* fine. For external hosted runners, we use an ephemeral deploy key on a bastion-forwarder and `docker -H ssh://git@bastion-proxy.corp.redwood` style push/pull through SSH tunnel, or we use our registry mirror service in public cloud for CI. DM me and I'll loop infra.
olivia: thanks everyone, happy to be here. Appreciate the quick help!
